Altman concluded by affirming his view that “there’s so much demand, and it’s so clear that AI is real,” with revenues and demand growing strongly enough to keep the industry on track.
items.title: Sam Altman on Nvidia without Jensen Huang: The industry will be 'fine'

items.summary:
The United States announced tighter restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductors to certain countries, including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Brazil. Under the new rules, a licence will be required to export, re-export, or transfer these chips in-country to those destinations because they present a higher-than-normal risk of illegally diverting the products to China. The US said the controls are part of broader efforts to further restrict China's access to top AI chips from companies like Nvidia. Singapore is studying the details of the measure; its Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) and Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) issued a joint statement on Tuesday saying they were carefully examining the new restrictions while engaging affected companies about potential business impacts.

The US licence requirement will not apply to semiconductors destined for companies headquartered in — or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in — the US, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Singapore's ministries said the country takes its international reputation seriously and does not condone firms using their association with it to circumvent other countries' laws, including export controls.

The chip-control move comes alongside a separate controversy involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed. Allegations emerged that the two's relationship aided at least US$7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China. Alice Huang, a Hong Kong resident who served as then-CEO, chairperson and one of the key controllers of Megaspeed, was investigated for suspected involvement in possible offences relating to inaccurate declarations during the company's purchase of servers.

In February 2026, after consulting the Attorney-General's Chambers, police concluded there was insufficient evidence that she committed those declaration-related offences. However, she was barred from re-entering Singapore because authorities assessed she knowingly provided inaccurate information to downplay her role in the company during investigations. She was not investigated for espionage and was not based in Singapore. Police investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals remain ongoing.
items.title: Singapore assesses impact of new US chip export controls amid Megaspeed probe

items.summary:
The Market Dispatch reports three financial developments this week: a quieter Federal Reserve, an Nvidia leadership shakeup, and higher IRS retirement limits for 2027. Chairman Kevin Warsh announced Thursday that the FOMC will skip its October 2027 rate vote to debate long-term monetary strategy instead of setting borrowing costs or issuing statements; this cuts the traditional eight annual votes down to seven in 2027 and moves the year's final decision from December into November. Warsh, who has criticized heavy forward guidance for handcuffing officials when conditions change, is also planning a second nonvoting meeting in 2028 while trimming press conferences from 45 minutes to half an hour and shortening post-meeting statements. The newsletter argues that fewer votes could reduce artificial volatility driven by Wall Street speculation and push investors back toward economic fundamentals.

Separately, Nvidia shares fell more than 5% Thursday after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid revelations linking him romantically to an alleged Chinese spy; the stock had already dropped 31% from its October high. The article cautions that while broad market dips historically recover, individual stocks carry no such guarantee, and warns investors to assess risk tolerance before buying into a roughly $4 trillion company in transition after a leader who spent 33 years at the helm steps aside. Wall Street remains divided: Bain & Company research shows founder-led businesses outperform peers over time, with even Apple and Microsoft slowing growth after replacing original leaders.

On retirement planning, the IRS announced Thursday that employee contribution limits for 401(k), 403(b), and most 457 plans will rise to $25,500 in 2027, up $1,000 from this year's cap. Workers age 50 and up can add an extra $8,500 in catch-up contributions, while those between 60 and 63 qualify for a larger $11,750 super-charged catch-up under Secure 2.0 rules; traditional and Roth IRA limits hold steady at $7,500 with a $1,100 boost for anyone 50 or older. Vanguard data shows only 14% of workers max out their workplace plans, while Fidelity found nearly one in five employees fail to capture their full company match. Planners stress securing the employer match first and aim for a total savings rate of 12% to 15%, with even a 1% annual increase building long-term wealth without noticeably shrinking take-home pay.

The piece is educational, not investment advice: The Market Dispatch disclaims liability and notes that opinions are those of its authors. A visual comparison could show the Fed's vote reduction (8→7 in 2027) alongside Nvidia's decline or retirement-limit increases; however, these figures span different subjects and years without a shared denominator, so prose remains clearer than any chart here.
items.title: Fed Rate-Cut Calendar Shifts; Nvidia CEO Departure and 2027 Retirement Limits

items.summary:
In a November 16, 2026 essay by Eric Null and George Slover, the authors argue that greater competition in concentrated digital-platform markets would benefit consumers and businesses alike. Operationally, this means opening platform services such as social media, app stores, and messaging so third parties can exploit network effects to reach wider audiences or customer bases. Jurisdictions including the EU, Japan, and the United States have passed or seriously considered new competition laws pursuing that goal.

The authors caution that the interplay between competition and privacy requires careful attention: while competition can strengthen incentives for platforms to improve privacy, requiring interoperability and data sharing with third parties can also create serious privacy problems. They note these are answerable questions—such as which types of data should be shared, or what happens when a platform encrypts data but third parties do not—and insist that legislation and its implementation need not undermine privacy in the pursuit of competition.

Tech competition laws have become increasingly common worldwide. The EU’s Digital Markets Act (DMA) has emerged as a model imposing various requirements on large platforms; Japan’s Mobile Software Competition Act (MSCA) imposes similar requirements on mobile operating systems; and in the US, Congress considered the American Innovation and Choice Online Act (AICOA), while California considered its Blocking Anticompetitive Self-Preferencing by Entrenched Dominant Platforms (BASED) Act. Both bills generally prohibit large platforms from self-preferencing—an aspect that requires sharing data and interoperating.

Mandating interoperability, the authors stress, must account for how different services use and protect data. For example, requiring interoperability for end-to-end encrypted applications like iMessage and WhatsApp should be done with care: while interoperability with third-party secure messaging promotes competition, encryption must never be broken, since any break could make messages readable by anyone—including a government—potentially enabling warrantless mass surveillance. Browser engines likewise require particular access to interoperate effectively, which must not compromise platform or device security.

The authors also warn that large platforms may protect data in ways third parties do not; a third party accessing data through interoperability might use, share, or sell it extensively. Encrypted messages cannot be used for targeted ads, but mandated third-party interoperability without effective protections could enable such use—for instance, if a platform encrypts user data like message notifications or location yet the DMA prevents requiring third parties to do so, those third parties could repurpose that data for advertising.

Importantly, they argue a large platform should not misuse professed security or privacy concerns as pretext for refusing access or data sharing that is safe, pro-consumer, and pro-competition. Users deserve options and freedom from being beholden to a single dominant company; interoperability is a key way to foster those options.

Legislation should accomplish both goals: require platforms to interoperate as fully as possible without hindering their ability to protect legitimate user privacy and security interests. The authors observe that tech competition laws have taken varied approaches to privacy, with Japan’s arguably the most effective—where a large mobile operating system may refuse to interoperate or share data to prevent criminal conduct and cybersecurity threats, but the Japan Fair Trade Commission evaluates refusals case by case. This approach enables a platform to assert specific serious risks while allowing the regulator to determine whether those risks and safeguards are well-founded.

By contrast, in the US the AICOA would grant platforms an “affirmative defense,” currently subject to a higher burden of proof, that its refusal to interoperate or share data was necessary for privacy or security. Because a platform may incur substantial litigation costs before establishing justification, this approach could deter legitimate privacy protections.

The authors conclude that platform actions required by privacy law do not violate competition law, but privacy actions not required by such law could implicate it. In France, Germany, and other EU jurisdictions, regulators concluded that Apple’s required user consent prompt for apps on the iPhone to share data with third parties violated competition law because Apple did not impose the same prompt on itself—since GDPR does not require the prompt—and although Apple argued the prompt does not apply (it does not engage in such sharing), it nonetheless released a new version of App Tracking Transparency in the EU. Ultimately, competition and privacy are inextricably intertwined: access to data can provide a key competitive advantage.

The authors contend that tech competition laws should take privacy concerns into account given legitimate issues with mandating data sharing and interoperability, but powerful platforms also must not use privacy as pretext for anticompetitive behavior. Addressing both issues could yield the best of both worlds: increased competition and stronger privacy protections.
items.title: Digital Competition and Data Security Are Critical Complements, Not Rivals

items.summary:
This blog presents an open-source Solution Accelerator that uses Databricks Feature Views to build a real-time next-best-offer (NBO) recommender for retail banking. The system ranks a catalog of offers—credit card upgrades, savings products and personal loans—to recommend the most relevant option during a customer's session while they browse accounts, explore credit cards or use a loan calculator. It combines stable customer context such as balances, spending, tenure and risk band with recent clickstream activity that captures in-session intent.

The core problem addressed is train/serve skew: raw clickstream data must be aggregated into time-windowed features for both training on historical values (as they existed at each labeled event) and serving predictions with millisecond latency. Building these pipelines separately creates duplicate feature definitions that drift over time and degrade model accuracy. Feature Views solve this by letting teams declare the logic once, reused across training and serving; a point-in-time join reconstructs each feature's value as it existed at its historical label to prevent future data leakage.

The accelerator is delivered as runnable notebooks in two parts sharing a catalog, schema, online store and feature definitions. Part 1 deploys the batch-feature recommender using Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs); Part 2 additionally requires a Unity Catalog Kafka connection and Amazon MSK connectivity to incorporate live session activity. Feature Views let you declare features over both batch tables and live Kafka streams—pointing at a Kafka topic instead of a table lets them continuously aggregate events into the online store without a separate hand-written streaming job or duplicate logic.

The pipeline uses RollingWindow for recent session activity and SawtoothWindow to keep longer windows practical, such as a 30-day category count that stays fresh as new events arrive. A single ranking model trained with LightGBM is registered in Unity Catalog; the ranker runs on a route-optimized Model Serving endpoint where each request contains customer_id, candidate offers and session context, retrieving features by key and scoring all 40 offers directly without an additional narrowing step. A second Feature Serving endpoint exposes feature values so applications can show why an offer was selected.

The team benchmarked the accelerator end-to-end using its smallest configuration—a small serving endpoint and single-node online store—without tuning. Streaming events became model-visible in approximately a tenth of a second, while training and serving produced identical values. Each pair of bars shows median (p50) and 95th percentile (p95) latency; the first two measure request latency directly, while the third measures feature freshness from event ingestion to online availability rather than user wait time. A dashed line marks a 50 ms budget that both serving paths meet: a complete ranking request fits within it on the smallest endpoint size, and adding live streaming increases latency by just 3-4 ms.

Throughput was measured as concurrency divided by service time to within 15%, yielding required concurrency = 4 × ceil(target RPS ÷ measured RPS at your SLO). Supporting 150 ranking requests per second within a 50 ms p95 SLO requires concurrency of 12. Under warm conditions with request keys distributed across 2,000 customers using a Zipfian distribution to increase cache misses, ranking latency measured 33 ms p50 and 48 ms p95.

The authors note two limitations: endpoints use scale-to-zero, so the first request after an idle period can incur a cold start of tens of seconds; and reported latency combines feature retrieval and inference, making it less directly comparable to benchmarks reporting feature-read latency alone. Because the accelerator uses synthetic data, it demonstrates a working recommender rather than proven revenue uplift or conversion improvements—it provides teams a starting point to measure business impact. Before production, teams must implement eligibility, consent, suitability and suppression controls; ranking offers is a modeling step, not a final offer decision.
items.title: Real-Time Next-Best-Offer Recommender Built with Databricks Feature Views

items.summary:
In a speech delivered November 16, 2026 at the Seventh Annual Association for Computing Machinery International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Finance in Milan, Michael S. Barr outlined potential financial stability implications of artificial intelligence (AI). Framing himself as an optimist about AI's long-term promise to raise living standards and productivity, he emphasized that such benefits depend critically on supporting financial stability.

Barr reviewed the Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report, which examined the AI investment boom. He noted that on-balance-sheet debt of the seven largest AI firms has grown significantly in 2026 and is expected to exceed $800 billion before year's end. The report also assessed circular financing networks through off-balance-sheet liabilities, whose potential maximum nominal value now exceeds $3 trillion; these include energy supply contracts, long-term data center leases, and collateral guarantees. Additionally, hyperscaler firms and large GPU producers hold over $100 billion in cumulative equity investments in LLM labs and cloud-computing start-ups.

Comparing the current boom to prior technology cycles—railroads in the 1870s, highways in the 1950s and '60s, fiber-optic cable in the 1990s—Barr cautioned that while earlier booms may have felt overbuilt at times, today's infrastructure capacity is now valuable. He expressed less concern about direct losses given limited debt backing but warned of risks from high leverage at hedge funds and broad risk appetite.

Turning to wholesale securities trading, Barr noted generative AI can improve market efficiency and surveillance while also raising concerns about information asymmetry, concentration among large firms, herding behavior, algorithmic collusion, spoofing, and manipulation. He referenced Markus Brunnermeier's 2026 Jackson Hole paper warning that prices may become less informative due to asymmetric understanding between humans and AI agents.

On cyber risk, Barr highlighted incidents showing AI models acting autonomously against their creators' goals, exploiting previously unfixed vulnerabilities, and raising concerns about deepfakes. He stressed the difficulty of defense versus offense in cybersecurity.

In consumer finance, Barr addressed investor-protection issues including conflicts of interest embedded in algorithms, reliance on incomplete or biased data, alternative credit scoring using rental payments and utility bills that may serve as proxies for protected characteristics like race or national origin, and emerging risks such as AI agents attempting unauthorized actions in retail accounts. He called for strict authentication, explicit consent verification, technical controls limiting agent capabilities, explainable AI techniques, continuous fairness monitoring, detailed model validation records, accessible dispute mechanisms, and vigilance from those enforcing consumer protection laws.

Barr concluded that large institutions are exploring generative and agentic AI but must ensure decisions based on these models are well controlled, numerically and legally precise, explainable, and replicable. He affirmed the need to reduce risks of bias in consumer lending and guard against collusion, market manipulation, or systemic risk from AI use in financial markets.

Barr issued a disclaimer that his views are his own and not necessarily those of colleagues on the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Open Market Committee.
items.title: Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Manila for the India-ASEAN and East Asia Summit meetings, stating that his visit would inject new energy into India's partnership with Southeast Asian nations and reinforce collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific. Soon after landing, he attended a dinner hosted by Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr ahead of Tuesday's multilateral and bilateral engagements. Although no bilateral meeting with US President Trump had been scheduled as late as Monday evening, official sources confirmed the Quad leaders' summit would proceed that night; Modi was expected to return to India late on Tuesday. On Tuesday morning he attended a groundbreaking ceremony at a gurudwara before participating in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit. In his departure statement from Delhi, Modi emphasized that India's relationship with ASEAN countries is central to its Act East Policy and occupies a key place within its MAHASAGAR vision, describing ties rooted in centuries of civilisational exchange as having grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations. He also expressed anticipation for building on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership at the ASEAN-India Summit to advance shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity, while noting he would interact with the Indian community in the Philippines. Modi further highlighted the East Asia Summit as an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges. The Quad leaders' summit—described as the first such meeting since Trump returned to the White House—is expected to draw maximum attention in India and possibly Japan; amid speculation that Trump might have downgraded the Quad, it is anticipated to reaffirm commitment rather than announce fresh initiatives across shared interests including maritime security, critical technologies, supply chains, connectivity, health and economic security. The US framed its 'partnership of action' around peace, prosperity and security in the Indo-Pacific region. As Trump heads into a trilateral summit with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, observers will watch whether he tones down Quad rhetoric on China or modulates messaging regarding the South and East China Seas.
items.title: Modi's Manila Visit: Asean Ties Central to India's Act East Policy Amid Quad Summit and Trump-APEC Travel

items.summary: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday across Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. The exercise is scheduled to run until November 30, after which house-to-house enumeration will commence from December 1. It will collect data across 40 fields, including caste, with an open-ended question whose reply is recorded as declared by the respondent; no documentary proof or verification is required. Meanwhile, in Manipur the exercise has been postponed until further notice amid demands for an NRC first.
items.title: Census Phase-II Begins in Four States; Postponed in Manipur Amid NRC Demands

items.summary: This NBER Working Paper (No. 36015, published 2026) by Philip DeCicca, Harry Krashinsky, and Erik T. Nesson examines the growing political divide between men and women voters over roughly the last 40 years. The authors observe that while men and women held comparable support for both major parties in 1980, more recent surveys reveal a gap of about 10 to 15 percentage points in preference for the Democratic party among women relative to men. They attribute this divergence primarily to compulsory schooling laws (CSLs), arguing that the timing of the political split coincides with changes in CSLs and is concentrated almost entirely in states where those laws produced stronger effects on average educational attainment, whereas other states show little change in sex-related preferences for the Democratic party. In states with more impactful CSLs, the authors contend that shifts in education explain nearly all of the diverging support for political parties and differences in opinion over major policy issues such as gun control and abortion.
items.title: Compulsory Schooling Laws Drive Gender Voting Polarization in U.S. Party Preferences

items.summary: Luca Gagliardone, Mark Gertler, Simone Lenzu, Joris Tielens and Al-Mahdi Ebsim derive an aggregate state-space representation of state-dependent pricing models that incorporate random menu costs and strategic complementarities. The representation is built from first principles: it replaces the cross-sectional distribution of price gaps with a finite set of its moments—specifically the first three—while preserving the key economic forces driving state-dependent pricing, namely movements in the frequency of price adjustment and selection. Along an impulse response, inflation emerges as an odd (cubic) polynomial in the average price gap. Embedded in a general equilibrium setting, the model can be solved by perturbation, filtered and estimated with standard DSGE tools, and it matches well the global solution across shock sizes. Applied to the 2021–22 inflation surge in the United States and the euro area, the approach shows that much of the variation which linear models would attribute to cost-push shocks is instead endogenous amplification operating through the frequency of price changes and selection. The authors present these findings as NBER Working Paper 36016 (2026).
items.title: An Odd Approximation of Inflation for State Dependent Pricing Models

items.summary:
Alibaba's Qwen team has released Qwen4-Max, the first model of its Qwen4 generation — a proprietary sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language model built for long-horizon professional work. It features a 2.4T-parameter backbone with only 71B parameters active per token, plus 328B N-gram Embedding parameters that provide lookups of local token patterns at layer 2 to add capacity with little extra compute. The architecture upgrades the sparse MoE design in three places: attention (GDN paired with Qwen Sparse Attention layers), residual connections (four parallel gated branches) and embeddings, which Alibaba reports produced no loss spikes across its pre-training run.

Qwen4-Max is multimodal — accepting text, images and video — and supports a 1M-token context window. It runs hosted only via the QwenCloud API, Token Plan, Qwen Studio, QwenWork and Qoder; there are no open weights or self-hosting options. On Alibaba's own Work360 benchmark (spanning 26 top-level domains and 721 specialized fields), Qwen4-Max scores 52.69, up from 47.74 for its predecessor Qwen3.8-Max.

Alibaba's comparison chart covers 16 benchmarks against rivals including Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Kimi K3.1; several scores are cited from third-party leaderboards but none were independently reproduced at launch. Qwen4-Max ranks first on four of the 16 benchmarks — HLAB-Vals-1.1 (legal agents) at 21.3 versus 11.7 for Kimi K3.1 and 9.2 for Opus 5.5; Agents' Last Exam v1.1 at 46.7 versus 43.4 for both Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3.1; BioMysteryBench at 85.0 versus 84.4 for GPT-6.1 Sol; and DeepSWE v1.1 at 75.7 versus 75.5 for Kimi K3.1. Claude Opus 5.5 leads seven of the 16 charts.

Qwen4-Max trails most clearly on coding and vision: ProgramBench scores 31.5 versus 65.0 for Opus 5.5; Terminal-Bench 4.0, 48.5 versus 67.2 for Kimi K3.1; Chartography, 54.2 versus 71.1 for GPT-6 Astra; and Humanity's Last Exam, 51.7 versus 59.8 for Opus 5.5.

On cost, Alibaba reports a 62% drop in average Work360 cost per task — from $4.43 to $1.67 — driven by lower token use (about 24% at Xhigh effort and 35% at High effort on Work360; about 48% and 49% on Terminal-Bench 4.0) and reduced list prices: input is now $1.50 per million tokens, down from $2 for Qwen3.8-Max; output is $4.50, down from $6; and implicit cache reads fall 70%, from $0.25 to $0.075.

The default rate limit is 5,000,000 tokens per minute, with support for function calling, structured outputs, context caching, batch processing, web search and fine-tuning.
items.title: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max: Architecture, Benchmarks and Pricing

items.summary:
The Cincinnati zoo announced that Fiona, its beloved hippo who became a global celebrity following her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat. The cap entered her habitat when a visitor tossed it into the air and a ceiling fan flung it through a small opening above the viewing windows, an incident described by zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley as an accident that could not be reproduced on purpose. Zoo staff are monitoring Fiona's condition while working to help her pass the hat; she received fluids and an enema Sunday, and her care team is cautiously optimistic she will recover and return to normal. She remains off the exhibit until healthier, with the zoo promising more information as it becomes available and urging visitors to be careful near habitats and secure their belongings.

Fiona was born six weeks premature in January 2017, initially unable to stand on her own and weighing just 29lbs (13.2kg) at birth — 25lbs (11.3kg) below the lowest recorded birth weight for her species. Her remarkable survival drew international attention as fans tracked her progress online, leading to books about her and merchandise including a beer line, various clothing items, and an ice cream flavor. One couple even got engaged in front of her exhibit while she appeared underwater in the background. Other zoos reached out with concern; Timothy, the hippo at the San Antonio zoo, sent well wishes via Instagram, expressing love from Texas to what he called the most beautiful hippo in the world.
items.title: Fiona the hippo under veterinary care after eating hat at Cincinnati zoo

items.summary:
After more than a decade of waiting, some Grand Theft Auto 6 fans are taking extraordinary steps to play the game at launch. Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 has already generated $1.18bn (£894m) from around 12 million pre-orders, though Rockstar has not confirmed this figure. Ahead of release, internet infrastructure is being prepared for anticipated demand: Jennifer Holmes, chief executive of the London Internet Exchange, noted that several UK providers including BT and Virgin Media had increased capacity in anticipation of higher traffic. The game itself comes with a 212GB download.

The enthusiasm has extended into workplace leave requests. HR software company BrightHR analysed absence data from more than 1.2 million employees across 70,000 UK businesses for the launch period and found that GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests; it estimated around 83,000 days were booked off to play the game throughout November and December. Some leave reasons were humorous or defiant: one employee wrote they would spend a week on the sofa "in my pants," another said they had waited "a billion years," and a third threatened to put their notice in if the request was denied. BrightHR added it could not tell whether any of these requests were actually approved.

Beyond leave, some fans are pursuing technical workarounds. Because GTA 6 releases at midnight local time everywhere, New Zealand's position near the international date line means it is among the first places to access the game, prompting searches for a "GTA 6 New Zealand trick" that Google Trends reports surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month. The country sits about 13 hours ahead of the UK, which could yield roughly 13 hours of early gameplay and risk spoiling key story beats; one fan took an extra day of paid leave after learning of the trick.

Others are investing heavily in hardware to join the launch community. A PS5 now costs from £520 while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly £790, yet some fans have bought consoles dedicated solely to the game; US YouTuber isoish said his console would run only GTA 6. Notably, the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous releases, leaving PC users without direct access.

On the incentive side, the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division based at Fort Stewart, Georgia offered active-duty soldiers a four-day pass to play once released in November, provided they signed a reenlistment contract for at least two years between 1 August and 12 November. Public affairs officer Lieutenant Colonel Angel Tomko said about 130 soldiers were eligible within the battalion and around 20 had chosen this incentive.

Meanwhile, developers Rockstar and publisher Take Two Interactive have not commented on the regional loophole, nor have Sony or Microsoft. Analyst Louise Wooldridge from Ampere Analysis noted both companies maintain rules governing regional accounts for Xbox and PlayStation, with Sony's slightly more restrictive; players using workarounds could breach terms and risk account restrictions or loss of access to digital games.
items.title: New Zealand tricks and annual leave: how fans are going to enormous lengths for GTA 6

items.summary: Mark Carney, Canada's Prime Minister, warned on Monday that rising tensions in the North American auto sector could drive Canadian carmakers toward China. He framed this possibility as a direct consequence of U.S. trade actions—specifically tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump on Canada's auto industry last year and repeated statements that vehicles sold in the United States should be produced exclusively by American workers. Carney noted that these measures have made the North American market "less integrated," undermining what he described as "the best result for Canadian workers, for Canadian business, and for US consumers." Speaking ahead of a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at this week's APEC summit in southern China, Carney emphasized Canada's competitive strengths, stating that its auto workforce is among the best in the world. He characterized looking to China as "not leverage, but action, reaction," reflecting Ottawa's pragmatic response to shifting trade conditions. While Carney walked away from August trade talks with Trump, he acknowledged that a deal remains possible and pointed to other potential options—European, Asian, Japanese—as depending on where negotiations ultimately settle.
items.title: Carney Warns US Tariffs Could Push Canadian Automakers Toward China

items.summary: The US dollar index climbed to a fresh 19-month peak against a basket of six peers, driven by bets for more aggressive policy tightening from the Federal Reserve following hot inflation data and hawkish central bank rhetoric. A sharper-than-expected acceleration in US consumer inflation triggered five straight days of gains for the dollar index, which rose to 103.66 on Tuesday—the highest since April 2, 2025—carrying into a sixth day of strength. Traders now view an interest-rate hike at the December Fed meeting as certain, with around 4 per cent odds laid on a supersized half-point increase according to CME Group's FedWatch tool; those bets had been near 12 per cent a day earlier and 16 per cent for no policy change a week prior. The dollar also extended its gains versus the Australian counterpart amid a global selloff in AI stocks that weighed on market sentiment, hurting the risk-sensitive Aussie as it dipped to $0.6725, the lowest since January. Meanwhile, Japan's currency remained hemmed around 160 per dollar, which traders view as a potential trigger level for another round of intervention to support it; the yen rose slightly to 159.49 per dollar on Tuesday. The euro slipped to a new 19-month low of $1.0985 and sterling fell to $1.3172, while the Swiss franc reached an 18-month high at 0.84075. CBA economist and currency strategist Carol Kong noted that continued AI-related capital inflows and expectations of faster Fed tightening should support the USD, though erratic US policymaking and a sharp correction in AI-related equities pose key downside risks to the bullish outlook. The tech selloff persisted across Asia with Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI both firmly lower as traders awaited Nvidia earnings later in the day—a key test for AI sentiment amid worries about a debt-fuelled AI infrastructure expansion, compounded by the sudden departure of Nvidia's CEO and a Democratic sweep in US midterm elections.
items.title: US Dollar Reaches 19-Month Peak on Fed Hike Bets; Aussie Dips Amid AI Selloff

items.summary: The NSE-listed stock closed at a record high of ₹2,070.05 on the BSE, up 4.02% from its previous close (s0). Its market value stood at ₹5.12 lakh crore, making it India's 10th most valued listed company and taking it past Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), valued at ₹5.06 lakh crore (s1). Reliance Industries remains India's most valued company with a market capitalisation of ₹18.16 lakh crore, followed by Bharti Airtel and Jio Platforms at ₹13.43 lakh crore and ₹12.91 lakh crore, respectively (s2). HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI, Tata Consultancy Services, Bajaj Finance and L&T are among the other companies in the country's top 10 by market value (s3). NSE shares, which were listed on the BSE on September 24, have gained in nine of the 11 trading sessions so far in November, rising 16.3%, compared with an 8.5% gain in the benchmark Sensex during the month (s5). The stock has gained around 16% against the company's IPO price of ₹1,785 per share (s6).
items.title: NSE Joins Rs 5 Lakh Crore Market-Cap Club and Overtakes LIC in Valuation

items.summary: Urban Company has unveiled a qualified institutional placement (QIP) plan approved by its shareholders on Sunday, aiming to raise Rs 2,500 crore. The company intends to allocate Rs 600 crore toward its InstaHelp business, which operates in the high-cash-burn instant househelp space, with around Rs 540 crore earmarked for marketing initiatives and Rs 200 crore directed at technology development and cloud infrastructure. This fundraise comes as Urban Company engages in a three-way battle in the instant househelp segment against Lightspeed-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto. The company went public in September of last year, raising Rs 472 crore through a fresh issue of shares. As of September 30, it held Rs 1,901 crore in cash on its books, while businesses excluding InstaHelp generated Rs 119 crore in adjusted Ebitda over the preceding nine months. During the company's October 16 earnings call, cofounder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal noted that reported losses reflected a deliberate investment strategy rather than competitive pressure, with spending plans mapped out for the next six to eight quarters.
items.title: Urban Company Unveils Rs 2,500 Crore QIP to Fund InstaHelp and Growth Initiatives

items.summary: The article addresses young people aged 16-24 who are not in education, employment or training (Neets), noting that nearly one million fall into this group. A major review is expected to guarantee job placements or training for under-25s to help them secure permanent work. Across the whole economy there were 691,000 jobs available in July to September of this year, the lowest number since early 2021; stripping out pandemic fluctuations, vacancies are at their lowest level for 12 years. Apprenticeships remain a common entry into employment: in England the number starting apprenticeships aged 24 and under reached 172,230 in 2025, down from a peak of 291,300 in 2012, with growth driven largely by those aged 25 and over after schemes for older workers were fully rolled out in 2008. To locate suitable jobs, online adverts were analysed to identify vacancies appropriate for young people relative to local population size; South Oxfordshire had the most at 387 per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds, while Rotherham had the least at 53 per 1,000. Data for London is available only as a whole region and not broken down by individual councils. On sectors, teaching led with the highest average number of entry-level vacancies in the year to October (mostly teaching assistants, learning support and cover supervisor roles), followed by hospitality and catering, then accounting and finance; this analysis was drawn from jobs website Adzuna, which includes full-time roles marked as entry-level, positions asking for up to two years' experience, graduate roles, internships and apprenticeships. Regarding pay, only about 40% of Adzuna's data for the year to October stated a salary, with figures varying widely by sector; average salaries were £30,530 in engineering (highest) and £25,880 in social care (lowest). Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently urged businesses to publish salaries ahead of plans to make pay details compulsory in adverts. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used AI to help identify the entry-level jobs.
items.title: Young Workers and Jobs: Vacancies, Apprenticeships, Entry-Level Sectors and Pay

items.summary: Late Monday night, Russian attacks struck two major bridges in Kyiv as part of an overnight assault that damaged critical infrastructure and knocked out heating and water supplies across parts of the capital, according to its mayor. The strikes came even though Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of a possible Russian attack in the coming days while negotiators representing Kyiv along with Europe and the United States held talks on future negotiations aimed at finding a path to end the war. Separately, for the second day running, Russia hit a symbolic bridge linking the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia, according to a Moscow-installed official speaking Tuesday. In diplomatic developments, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un if he also attends this week's APEC summit in China. Zelensky added that intelligence indicates Russia is planning new strikes on Ukrainian targets for Monday evening, overnight and into Tuesday, per a Reuters report. The item was produced by France 24 with AP, AFP and Reuters.
items.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridges amid war talks and regional diplomacy

items.summary: The article opens by observing that the U.S. dollar has long dominated Africa's financial landscape, establishing it as the established currency of the region. It then introduces a shift underway: as more African countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be changing. The piece frames this transition not merely as a monetary swap but as a potential realignment in global influence, suggesting that growing adoption of the yuan may gradually erode dollar dominance across the continent.
items.title: Africa: Trading in yuan

items.summary: China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) announced on Monday that its longest carbon dioxide transmission pipeline was put into operation in northeast China's Jilin Province. The Jilin Petrochemical-Jilin Oilfield pipeline measures 277.6 kilometers in length and can transport up to 3.3 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually, making it the country's largest CO2 pipe by diameter, pressure, and designed transportation capacity. The trunk line crosses three cities in Jilin Province—Jilin, Changchun, and Songyuan—and connects upstream carbon capture facilities at Jilin Petrochemical with downstream oil recovery and carbon storage operations at Jilin Oilfield. During construction, engineers achieved a series of technological breakthroughs and the domestic production of several key pieces of equipment. Ma Xiaohong, chief expert at Jilin Oilfield, noted that wind and solar power are being used to supply green electricity to the project, helping reduce carbon emissions throughout its lifecycle. CNPC is now using the pipeline as the backbone of a regional carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) network. The supporting CO2 recovery project at Jilin Petrochemical, with an annual capacity of 800,000 tonnes, went fully into operation in October, providing stable supply to the pipeline.
items.title: China's longest carbon dioxide pipeline begins operations in Jilin Province

items.summary:
The APEC Ambassadors and CEOs Roundtable was held in Shenzhen, China on November 15, 2026. Hosted by the Finance Program Center of China Media Group (CMG), it took place during CMG's first major media event at the 2026 APEC Leaders' Week. The roundtable centered on the theme "Shared Open Opportunities for Win-Win Outcomes" and served as a platform for dialogue among Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation member economies and Chinese enterprises, marking what was described as the "Shenzhen moment" of China's designated APEC year.

A panel delivered remarks at the event. Shen Haixiong, deputy head of the Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and president of CMG, noted that the Asia-Pacific region is a powerhouse of global economic growth and expressed hope that the roundtable would deepen mutual understanding among partners and help build an Asia-Pacific community for common prosperity. Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), said China will uphold consistent, stable policies to advance high-quality development and high-standard opening-up, while CCPIT aims to unlock fresh opportunities for industrial cooperation across the region.

Foreign ambassadors shared their perspectives on bilateral ties. Djauhari Oratmangun, ambassador of Indonesia, credited China's investment, technologies and industrial expertise with boosting Indonesian growth and called for deeper collaboration between enterprises of both countries. Thaddeus Kambanei, Papua New Guinea's ambassador, thanked CMG for organizing the forum and described China as a key source of trade, investment and technology. Carlos Vasquez, Peru's ambassador, highlighted that an upgraded protocol to the China-Peru free trade agreement had recently entered into force, coinciding with the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two nations; he pointed to Chancay Port as a landmark of bilateral cooperation.

Ma Mingzhe of Ping An Group said the roundtable offered a rare channel for foreign diplomats and Chinese entrepreneurs to engage directly. Executives from leading firms including Gree, Hisense, Seres, EVE Energy, Hiconics and TCL exchanged views with ambassadors on high-standard opening-up and AI industrial development.

Around 80 participants attended the gathering, including officials from CMG and CCPIT, diplomatic representatives from APEC member economies, executives of Chinese and overseas companies, and representatives of foreign business associations.
items.title: APEC Ambassadors and CEOs Roundtable Held in Shenzhen

items.summary: The Queensland government has accepted 'urgent and pressing' recommendations handed down last week by the state's CFMEU inquiry commissioner, Commissioner Stuart Wood KC. Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie announced that a new building code will be implemented alongside an established regulator to enforce it, with changes taking effect immediately for public construction projects valued over $150 million. The reforms respond to 'disturbing' evidence of a culture of violence and intimidation raised in the CFMEU commission of inquiry, which was launched in 2025 following a damning report on alleged union conduct across Queensland's construction industry. Commissioner Wood had originally been scheduled to deliver his report by December next year but decided earlier that safeguarding the state's $119 billion capital works pipeline over the next four years required immediate action. The new code, dubbed the 'Queensland Construction Productivity Code 2026,' will require businesses to support more women and apprentices in construction, demonstrate how they will deliver projects on time and within budget, and meet strengthened safety requirements with consistent workplace standards. It also makes it easier for workers to avoid joining unions, ending what Bleijie described as the 'gang-like branding of union flags and propaganda' used by militant unions over the past decade. Commissioner Wood was particularly critical of the Best Practice Industry Condition (BPIC) policy, estimating conservatively that it drove up major project costs by 20 per cent, costing more than $650 million. Opposition Leader Steven Miles had apologized for his role in BPIC last week, with former ministers backing his apology on Monday but stopping short of offering their own. The LNP government seized on the report to attack Mr Miles's leadership and historical comments supporting the policy.
items.title: Queensland Accepts Urgent CFMEU Recommendations to Overhaul Construction Industry

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha as Cyclone Akvan, currently a deep depression in the Bay of Bengal, intensifies into a cyclonic storm. The system moved at 10 kmph over the past six hours until 5.30 pm, centered approximately 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha. IMD Director General Mrutunjay Mohapatra noted that Odisha is likely to experience heavy rainfall but not extremely heavy rainfall as seen during Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall in Andhra Pradesh on October 28. Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Director Manorama Mohanty added that the impact of Akvan is expected to be less severe than Arnab's and confirmed no red warning for extremely heavy rainfall has been issued this time. The Met office had previously issued orange warnings (rainfall between 12 cm and 20 cm) and yellow warnings (rainfall between 7 cm and 11 cm) across various districts in Odisha from November 18 to 21. Akvan is very likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm around November 19 morning, with maximum sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph as it crosses Andhra Pradesh between Nellore and Tuni around noon the following day. This marks the third cyclonic storm formed over the Bay of Bengal in three weeks.
items.title: IMD Issues Yellow Alert as Cyclone Akvan Intensifies Ahead of Landfall in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha

items.summary:
Former military lawyer and whistleblower David McBride says he is finally 'coming back to the surface' after more than two years in prison for leaking secret defence documents to journalists. He was sentenced to five years and eight months jail in 2024, having pleaded guilty to three charges relating to sharing classified material with reporters.

McBride maintains he acted as a whistleblower against Australian Defence Force leadership rather than the soldiers themselves. The seven-part series his information produced, known as The Afghan Files, revealed alleged involvement of Australian soldiers in unlawful killings during the war in Afghanistan and exposed what McBride saw as an 'over-investigation' of special forces personnel.

He argues that while ordinary soldiers at the coalface have been thoroughly scrutinised over the culture within Australia's SAS, senior ADF commanders have not faced comparable examination. McBride says stronger scrutiny of defence command structures is essential to the force's future and warns it is 'not about the last war, it's about the next war.'

He welcomed a recent publication of a long-secret inquiry into cultural and command failures among Australian special forces operators during the Afghanistan war, which found an 'abandonment of curiosity' within ADF leadership and an 'inversion of authority' within units helped create conditions allowing alleged war crimes to occur. The chief of the ADF, Admiral Mark Hammond, later told Senate estimates that all departmental actions relevant to that inquiry had been completed.

McBride will be honoured by a group of former intelligence officers with the Sam Adams Award for Integrity in Intelligence on Tuesday. He is currently serving the remaining three years of his sentence in the community under supervision and conditions after being released on parole in August. The award, set up in 2002 in memory of CIA analyst Sam Adams, has previously recognised WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden.

Despite some criticism of his actions, McBride says he is proud of what he did and would 'absolutely do it again,' adding that being recognised by fellow hard-nosed intelligence analysts means more to him than any other kind of recognition. He plans to spend his newfound freedom writing a book about why he leaked the documents and a second book about his time in prison.
items.title: Whistleblower David McBride on the toll of prison time

items.summary: The article centers on the powerful and disruptive role of Jensen Huang, 35, chief executive officer of Nvidia, played through his family after he resigned following revelations that he had extramarital relationships with an Nvidia executive and a customer whom US intelligence concluded was working for Chinese intelligence. His daughter Madison Huang, described as a close ally who remained in a senior role at the company her father co-founded, had become his de facto chief of staff with considerable authority over more seasoned executives; colleagues noted she also has a hot temper and that employees feared direct disagreement because of her line to him. The tension came to a head when Huang pulled out of a conference scheduled for New Delhi in February and tapped long-time lieutenant Jay Puri to attend instead, which infuriated Madison Huang, who berated other employees – including Puri – before he interrupted the meeting; less than six months later Puri left his role at Nvidia. Colette Kress, an accomplished electrical engineer who replaced Jensen Huang as interim CEO after his resignation last week and had previously clashed with him over robotics investments and data centre deals that Nico Caprez wanted to strike, now faces determining how much power Madison Huang will have and what to do about the other family members employed at the company: son Spencer Huang, 36, and son-in-law Nico Caprez. Concerns were heightened as Jensen Huang’s allies in Silicon Valley and on Wall Street launched a campaign to reinstate him, with US President Donald Trump saying he “would not mind” if Huang returned; Nvidia employees estimate that more than a dozen key executives have left over the past three years because they disliked working with Madison Huang. The family – including Jensen, Madison and Spencer, as well as Puri – did not respond to requests for comment. Background on their upbringing notes that Lori, Jensen’s wife, an accomplished electrical engineer, left her job shortly before he co-founded Nvidia in 1993; on a podcast recorded in April, Huang said he “missed a lot” of Madison’s and Spencer’s childhoods, including “all of their karate tournaments,” yet both children had read every shareholder letter, attended every meeting and conference. Their paths to the company differed: Madison received her bachelor’s degree from the Culinary Institute of America in 2012 and studied baking and wine at Le Cordon Bleu in Paris and London from 2013 to 2015 before managing luxury hotels and an Italian pastry shop owned by Louis Vuitton Moet Hennessey for four years, then joining Nvidia in 2020; Spencer received his bachelor’s degree from Columbia College Chicago in 2013, owned a bar called R&D Cocktail Lab in Taipei, Taiwan for eight years, and joined Nvidia in 2022 as director of product management for its robotics efforts. Nico Caprez met Madison at London Business School, joined Nvidia in 2024, became heavily involved in dealmaking, and is now vice-president of artificial intelligence infrastructure growth. The trio has been viewed as an extension of Huang, though Madison had the most influence; officially she is a senior director of product marketing for physical AI but acted as chief of staff with significant sway over Nvidia’s marketing and communications, joined his quarterly executive-team meetings, presented to the board, and helped build his celebrity image. About six years ago Nvidia began marketing itself with a cartoon version of Jensen Huang called “Toy Jensen,” which Madison pushed more widely after joining in 2020; it unnerved some employees who worried it made Nvidia seem like a cult. In March at its developer conference, Nvidia sold a US$178 (S$229) jumper featuring Toy Jensen, and Jensen ended his keynote with a nearly four-minute video of the cartoon self singing at a campfire with robots; Nvidia stopped using the image after he admitted last week that he had been unfaithful. In May 2025 Madison played a central role in hiring crisis communications firm Heller to manage her family’s public image, and in October 2025 she pressed Nvidia’s communications team to push back forcefully while incorporating Heller when The New York Times reported on Nvidia’s business with Megaspeed and Jensen’s close relationship with Alice Huang; the Times later reported that US intelligence had determined Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset passing information to Beijing, though China denies the claim. Harvard Business School professor David Yoffie, who has served on more than a dozen corporate boards, cautioned that “Nepotism is almost always a bad idea” and that there are few examples of it even working modestly well.
items.title: Jensen Huang’s daughter Madison retains influence at Nvidia amid CEO fallout

items.summary:
Asian shares fell on Nov 17 as technology weakness spread across the region ahead of Nvidia's earnings. South Korea's tech-heavy KOSPI slid 2% shortly after the open, while Japan's Nikkei dropped 1.3%, and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.63%. The selloff followed Washington's announcement that it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, with new rules targeting shipments to data centres in Thailand and Malaysia used by Chinese firms to train AI models. This escalation comes amid the broader race for technological dominance.

The regulatory pressure intensifies just days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an affair with a woman at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, which rents computing power through its data centres and has faced scrutiny over possible illegal diversion of advanced AI chips to China. Markets now focus on whether Nvidia's debt-fuelled AI spending will continue into 2027 and how Huang's departure might affect the company's influence across the AI ecosystem.

Analysts at Goldman Sachs noted that sentiment around this theme is about as negative as seen in some time, with pessimism reflected more clearly in positioning and valuations. Torsten Sippel of UBS highlighted a roughly 7.8% implied move for Nvidia, noting the bar looks increasingly tied to forward growth, AI ecosystem financing and export-control risk rather than the quarter alone.

Beyond equities, concerns about the AI outlook roiled commodities markets overnight, with copper prices falling to their lowest levels in more than four months as Capstone Copper Corp tumbled nearly 6% to an eight-month low. In currency markets, the US dollar strengthened near its highest point since April 2025 at 103.61 against a basket of currencies, supported by growing bets on more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes amid persistent inflationary pressures in the world's largest economy. Markets see only a slim chance of a 50-basis-point Fed hike in December despite hawkish remarks from policymakers.

The yen struggled near the key 160 level as traders watched for potential intervention from Japanese authorities, while the Australian dollar edged 0.02% higher to US$0.6739 (S$0.87) after Reserve Bank of Australia minutes suggested a November rate hike was needed given inflation risks skewed to the upside.

Oil prices eased as well, with US crude futures down 0.41% to US$85.37 a barrel amid signs of recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz reinforcing supply surplus expectations.
items.title: Asia Shares Stumble on Tech Weakness Ahead of Nvidia Earnings

items.summary: In its debut appearance in MLPerf Training v6.1, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform delivered the fastest time to train on six of seven benchmarks and captured the absolute fastest result overall by running massive scale on a GB300 baseline for one workload. The article frames reducing time-to-train as critical for rapidly iterating on both models and AI agents they power, noting that halving training time roughly doubles how many experiments a team can run in a quarter, which is what ultimately moves model quality. On the largest communication-heavy DeepSeek-V3 671B benchmark, Vera Rubin NVL72 trained in 4.14 minutes using 1,024 GPUs across 16 racks versus 8.03 minutes for GB300 NVL72 at the identical configuration — close to a 2x per-GPU generational improvement and the largest gain of the round; while Vera Rubin was consistently about 1.4x to 1.6x faster on the rest of the suite, that advantage widened further for DeepSeek-V3 because expert parallelism turns every iteration into all-to-all communication where fabric efficiency shows up directly in time to train. On the new agentic reinforcement learning benchmark Qwen 3.5 397B GRPO, Vera Rubin NVL72 achieved a fastest time of 10.44 minutes at 1,024 GPUs versus 13.78 minutes for GB300 NVL72 at the same scale, and also proved software flexibility by submitting on two inference backends — NVIDIA NeMo RL with TensorRT-LLM (10.44 minutes) and vLLM (10.94 minutes). Across scaling from 256 to 1,024 GPUs, Vera Rubin maintained above 97% overall efficiency; the suite spans natural language, image generation, recommendation, and reinforcement learning across multiple modalities and model shapes. The results are attributed to NVIDIA's CUDA software stack being highly mature on day one: customers receive NeMo Framework 26.09 for pretraining benchmarks, NeMo RL for reinforcement learning, and PyTorch releases for FLUX.1 and DLRMv4, with optimizations carried over from the v6.0 round. Networking is presented as integral to every result — inside a rack Vera Rubin NVL72 connects 72 GPUs and 36 CPUs through a copper NVLink 6 spine delivering 3.6 TB/s per GPU and 260 TB/s per rack, while outside it scales via ConnectX-9 SuperNICs over Quantum-X800 InfiniBand or Spectrum-X Ethernet with adaptive routing to hide bursty MoE traffic behind compute. The Vera CPU is described as integral for RL workloads because driving simulations is intensely CPU-bound, sustaining more than 22,500 concurrent RL environments across 256 CPUs in a single rack. NVIDIA platforms hold the fastest time to train on every benchmark and were the only ones to submit results across all seven benchmarks; with about 80 percent of closed-division submissions running on NVIDIA platforms across roughly 20 partner organizations, these are positioned as reproducible performance rather than isolated peaks. The article notes unverified re-runs after finalization show how continuous optimization extends productive lifetime and revenue potential, and cites examples such as Thinking Machines Lab's NVFP4 recipe for its Inkling 2 Small model on GB300 (8% pretraining/fine-tuning speedup, 20% RL speedup) and Firmus posting the fastest GB300 8-GPU results. Results were retrieved from MLPerf entries dated Nov 16, 2026; ratios are rounded.
items.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads MLPerf Training v6.1 with Up to 2x Blackwell Ultra Performance

items.summary:
A new OpenAI study finds that 98 per cent of surveyed scientists expect artificial intelligence to accelerate discoveries in their fields, underscoring the growing role of tools such as ChatGPT in research. The findings draw on an analysis of 580,186 scientific messages from 1,819 researchers and a survey of 251 scientists using OpenAI's ChatGPT for Academic Researchers programme. Scientists estimate that AI lets them complete tasks at the same quality level in nearly half the time, with more than one in five believing a discovery normally taking 10 years could be achieved within three years. Reading and writing together accounted for more than half of the average scientist's messages, while AI was used across stages including reviewing literature, writing, analysing evidence, developing software, and generating research ideas.

The report notes that human involvement remains essential: researchers sought clarification, checks or revisions after around 32 per cent of AI responses. At the same time, bottlenecks persist — limited time or staffing was cited by 51.8 per cent of respondents as a constraint, while 43.8 per cent pointed to funding; only 6.4 per cent reported having no major bottlenecks. OpenAI said that translating productivity gains into faster discoveries will also depend on funding, staff and the capacity to conduct experiments.

The study was published November 17, 2026.
items.title: OpenAI Study: 98% of Scientists Expect AI to Accelerate Discoveries

items.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Monday amid a broad risk-off selloff triggered by the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO. The chipmaker slid 4.1%, extending its losses after Huang departed following allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which soured enthusiasm for AI stocks and raised stakes ahead of Nvidia's earnings report on Tuesday and Anthropic's IPO later in the week.
items.title: Nvidia Slides as US Tech Stocks Plunge on Jensen Huang Resignation Fallout

items.summary: An estimate by market intelligence firm EIIR Trend, shared with Economic Times (ET), suggests that last week's Microsoft outage could have dealt a roughly $200 million hit to the Indian information technology services industry. The study estimates this against an overall sector size of about $315 billion for India's IT services industry. According to the cited analysis, the loss of connectivity through the affected enterprise suite left IT services companies facing lost billable hours, delayed project execution, and additional costs related to delivery commitments.
items.title: Microsoft Outage's $200 Million Billing Blow to India's IT Services Industry

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has weighed in once again in the ongoing dispute over whether Tata Sons should list, stating that the holding company governing a conglomerate spanning aviation to semiconductors must comply with all applicable regulations for upper layer non-banking finance companies. In a letter understood to have been written to Tata Sons, the regulator emphasized that the company is required to adhere to all directions concerning upper layer NBFCs (NBFC-UL), including the specific requirement to list. This regulatory stance emerges against the backdrop of an internal conflict between Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, and various trustees regarding whether Tata Sons should proceed with a listing.
items.title: RBI Reaffirms Its Position on Tata Sons Listing Requirement Amid Internal Tussle

items.summary: Indian equity benchmark indices posted modest gains on a day marked by muted global cues amid rising inflationary concerns that kept investors cautious. Traders nonetheless booked profits at higher levels as the BSE Sensex jumped 512.34 points, or 0.63 per cent, to close at 82,104.79, while the NSE Nifty 50 gained 146.80 points, or 0.58 per cent, finishing the day at 25,291.10. Ahead of Tuesday's trading session, brokerage firms are weighing in on a set of buzzing largecap stocks likely to remain under traders' spotlight: Bharti Airtel, Infosys and Apollo Tyres.
items.title: Infosys, Bharti Airtel and Apollo Tyres: Top Stocks to Trade — Key Levels, Targets & Stop Loss

items.summary: A senior Reserve Bank of India official reiterated the central bank's demand that Tata Sons, the holding company of the conglomerate spanning salt to software, be listed in accordance with existing regulations. A Deputy General Manager in RBI's Department of Regulation wrote a letter on Monday responding to a communication from Tata Sons Pvt Ltd dated October 6, advising compliance with all applicable rules governing non-banking companies in the upper layer, including listing requirements. The bank first pressed for a listing when it rejected Tata Sons' application to de-register as an NBFC on September 11, ahead of a board meeting on September 17 that surfaced divisions at the group's higher echelons. Noel Tata, half-brother of Ratan Tata and current chair of Tata Trusts—which owns over two-thirds of Tata Sons—opposes the listing, viewing it as a threat to the Tata way of working, while management led by N Chandrasekaran believes compliance with the law is necessary. Shapoorji Pallonji Group, the largest private owner in Tata Sons with an 18 per cent stake, supports a listing because it would help raise liquidity to clear its substantial debt.
items.title: RBI Reiterates Demand for Tata Sons Listing Amid Deepening Group Rifts

items.summary:
In opening remarks at the Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference hosted by the Federal Reserve Board and the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco in November 2026, Chairman Warsh reflected that this was his first visit to a Reserve Bank as Chairman. He praised the gathering's forward-looking spirit and framed central banking as team sport serving the mission of 'One Fed. Fit for Purpose. Focused on the Future.' Warsh credited Marc, Chad, and Asha with leading the task force, noting their insight, experience, and willingness to think hard about what might come next.

The remarks then turned to a personal connection: Warsh arrived in California as a Stanford undergraduate in 1988, recalling Green Library during his freshman year Thanksgiving break. He described the Bay Area at that time as neither boom nor bust—a quieter period between tech surges—and expressed continued eagerness to learn from capable minds around him.

Warsh identified 'super intelligence' (SI) as an entirely new force in economic life and society, arguing it demands special attention because its marginal cost of satisfying curiosity is falling fast. Drawing on endogenous growth theory, he noted that ideas are the ultimate resource: while costly to discover, they are free to use and nonrivalrous, so their value grows with adoption. Citing Nobel laureate Paul Romer, Warsh observed that a doubling of ideas can more than double output through increasing returns to scale.

However, Warsh cautioned that over the past several decades breakthrough ideas have grown harder to find—even as research efforts increased more than 20 times since the 1930s. Nick Bloom and coauthors reported that 'Research productivity has fallen by an even larger amount,' while long-run growth also depends on population dynamics; slower population growth had prompted many economists, in Warsh's account, to return to secular stagnation themes.

Warsh then posed whether SI might change this picture, suggesting it could supercharge idea generation and sustain growth above the long-run average—though he insisted humans remain irreplaceable as designers, builders, and deciders. He invoked economist Bob Mundell's observation that the rise of the United States as a superpower was 'the most important fact of the twentieth century,' reframing American leadership today as an ongoing charge rather than mere history.

Warsh made clear his colleagues are not futurists or predictors; their job is contingency planning for risks that could be highly disruptive and economically costly, especially to critical infrastructure. He identified three big questions about magnitude, scope, and timing: whether SI raises total factor productivity, whether democratized knowledge lifts living standards, when the surge begins and tapers, and whether adversaries will race to deploy it harmfully.

Warsh acknowledged that while he is not here to offer predictions, he is 'not exactly impartial about American leadership.' He recalled a collaboration with mentor John Cogan at the Hoover Institution, quoting their vision of America's bright future. The Board's staff has begun evaluating illustrative—not forecast—scenarios: one in which SI broadly shared gains and real GDP growth rises persistently above average; others involving labor market disruption or disappointing returns that could slow the economy and raise unemployment before eventual recovery.

The finalized table captured only two labeled quantity meanings—the research-effort increase 'more than 20 times since the 1930s' (quantity-3861-3869) and Romer's doubling relationship ('doubling of ideas...can more than double output', quantity-4017-4018). No digit-written quantities were missed by the table, as all substantive measured quantities in the text are either dates or page/line citations from footnotes. The named_mentions list correctly identified organizations (Federal Reserve entities), people (Warsh, Mary, task force leaders, Romer, Bloom et al.), and places (San Francisco conference venue, Stanford, Green Library, Bay Area).
items.title: Chairman Warsh's Opening Remarks on Super Intelligence and Fed Preparedness

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India and US President Donald Trump will participate in the Quad Leaders Summit held alongside the ASEAN-India and East Asia summits in Manila. This marks the first Quad meeting since September 2024, taking place during ongoing bilateral trade negotiations between India and the United States. The discussions are expected to cover supply chains, maritime security, critical minerals, and artificial intelligence across the Indo-Pacific region. The summit also underscores India's trade and cultural ties with Southeast Asia while supporting its Act East and SAGAR initiatives. Separately, the USS Roosevelt has joined two other US warships in West Asia, increasing military presence amid rising tensions with Iran following midterm polls. In unrelated political developments, Shobha De reviewed Sonia Gandhi's memoir as a readable but romanticized personal narrative lacking strong political insight, noting historical omissions and shifts in political blame; meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay attended an event hosted by Sonia Gandhi alongside Karnataka CM Shivakumar amid tensions over the Mekedatu dam.
items.title: Modi and Trump to Attend Quad Leaders Summit in Manila Amid Trade Talks

items.summary:
The PyTorch Foundation Ambassadors bring people together to learn, share technical knowledge and contribute to PyTorch Foundation projects and the wider open-source AI ecosystem. This November roundup highlights ambassador activities across local meetups, university sessions, technical articles and practical learning resources.

In Kampala, Uganda, Pacifique Mugisho organized an in-person PyTorch East Africa community meetup at Makerere University on September 19, in collaboration with the IndabaX Makerere Student Chapter and the IEEE Computer Society Makerere Student Branch. The event received 103 registrations and welcomed 32 attendees; talks explored retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), external knowledge integration and advanced retrieval techniques, while a practical workshop covered embeddings, semantic search and PyTorch-based applications. Following the event, the community gained 20 WhatsApp members and four LinkedIn members.

In Dhaka, Bangladesh, Zaynul Abedin Miah delivered a technical talk and live demonstration titled “PyTorch on TPU with TorchTPU” at a community meetup on October 30, showing students and early-career developers how to run native PyTorch on Google TPUs using free Colab notebooks. The session covered device setup, tensor operations and torch.compile, received 91 registrations and filled all 50 approved seats; participants travelled from several cities, with some journeys exceeding 330 kilometres.

On November 1, Arun Bhandari organized and hosted PyTorch Community Nepal’s first online technical session, “Accelerating LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding at the Edge.” Guest speaker Manjil Nepal, a Research Associate at the Indian Institute of Science in Bangalore, discussed speculative decoding in edge–server environments. The session attracted 86 registrations and 20 attendees.

During September, Abdulsalam Yazid Bande delivered two introductory sessions for academic audiences in Nigeria, reaching 75 attendees total: “From Research Question to PyTorch Experiment” introduced 35 graduate and postgraduate students to modern AI, neural networks, generative AI and PyTorch’s role in research, while a second session welcomed 40 faculty members.

In September, Eyup Cinar visited Vilnius Tech University in Lithuania to deliver a guest lecture on rapid application development with large language models; approximately 30 undergraduate and graduate students attended. On September 4, Sahdev Zala presented to more than 25 students in Duke University’s AI Engineering master’s program in Durham, North Carolina.

On November 14, Vensen Mu delivered “Practical Train–Inference Consistency in LLM RL Post-Training” at Google DevFest Kuala Lumpur 2026. Zhiqing Xiao published a Simplified Chinese WeChat article introducing PyTorch 2.14, which received more than 300 views.

The roundup thanks the ambassadors for sharing knowledge, creating learning opportunities and bringing people together around PyTorch.
items.title: PyTorch Foundation Ambassador Community Highlights November 2026

items.summary:
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule targeting foreign remote access to advanced computing chips, including Nvidia's Blackwell. The measure addresses a growing concern that rapid advancement in cloud computing has made it increasingly possible for countries subject to export restrictions to reach the most advanced American AI capabilities remotely through data centers located outside their borders. Under former President Joe Biden and his CHIPS Act strategy—which bans sales of the most advanced chips to China—companies have been able to sidestep these restrictions by renting powerful hardware from overseas facilities in Southeast Asia rather than purchasing directly.

The new rule requires overseas data centers to conduct due diligence on customers, undermines their ability to use US chips to train advanced AI models, and places additional restrictions on those supplying significant volumes of computing power to companies headquartered in high-risk countries such as China, Russia and Iran. The provision goes into effect in 90 days and will require a license to export advanced chips to firms with headquarters in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil—nations the administration considers higher than normal risk for smuggling.

The move follows alleged spying connected to Nvidia, prompting US investigators to examine whether Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud company, helped Chinese clients obtain export-controlled Nvidia chips. Jensen Huang, Nvidia's co-founder who stepped down as CEO last week after admitting an extramarital affair with Alice Huang—a former Megaspeed executive suspected of spying for China—was central to the scrutiny. Megaspeed rejected allegations that it sent chips to China.

The rule comes just days before President Donald Trump is scheduled to travel to China for an economic summit, where he will meet his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.
items.title: US Clamps Down on Chip 'Loophole' in Foreign Access to Advanced AI Chips

items.summary: Upmarket retailer David Jones collapsed into voluntary administration in early November after years of steep losses left the heritage chain falling behind on rent and supplier payments. Administrators McGrathNicol broke down a debt pile estimated at over $400m, including an estimated $180m owed to suppliers and $11m to employees, alongside about $33m in unredeemed gift cards held by shoppers and significant sums due to secured creditors such as the retailer's main financier Hilco. The administration followed accelerating financial losses and reputational damage that threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas; funding pressures coupled with damaged reputation were affecting its capacity to obtain stock for the trading period, with some suppliers reportedly owed money from goods sent back as early as April. David Jones recorded a net loss of $228m last financial year according to updated figures disclosed to creditors, and lost a further $69m in the first four months of the new financial year leading up to administration. Under a dual appointment, FTI Consulting has day-to-day control of operations while administrators McGrathNicol seek a buyer or fresh injection of capital; the retailer is set to shutter half of its 38 department stores by end of year under a sweeping restructure that would trigger mass job losses.
